key_insight: Variational quantum algorithms reproduce graphene and nanoribbon band structures, but hardware noise limits useful circuit depth and energy agreement alone can mask wavefunction errors.
engineering_relevance: The workflow provides a validated NISQ baseline and non-interacting reference states for future simulations of correlated materials.
method: Map graphene and nanoribbon Bloch Hamiltonians in the p_z tight-binding approximation to Pauli operators.
Use VQE for the ground band and VQD for excited subbands.
Validate against exact diagonalization and assess wavefunctions with a subspace-containment diagnostic.
evidence_signal: Ideal simulations closely match exact diagonalization; deeper ansatz circuits improve ideal accuracy by over three orders of magnitude but worsen noisy energy estimates, with hardware deviations of a few hundredths of the hopping parameter.
watch_item: Logarithmic qubit scaling with ribbon width does not ensure accuracy: fixed-depth ansatz performance degrades as the Hilbert space grows.
paper_title: Band structure of two-dimensional graphene and of one-dimensional nanoribbons via variational quantum algorithms: from energies to wavefunction quality
